Contract.title: Contract
Contract.description: Represents a legal contract document and its associated metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Contract entity.

title.description: The title or name of the contract.

description.description: A brief summary or description of the contract's purpose.

documentId.description: Reference to the Document entity, pointing to the contract's full text. (Relationship: Contract 1:1 Document)

status.description: The current status of the contract (e.g., 'Draft', 'Active', 'Expired', 'Terminated').

effectiveDate.description: The date on which the contract becomes effective.

expirationDate.description: The date on which the contract expires.

renewalDate.description: The date on which the contract is up for renewal.

companyId.description: Reference to the Company involved in the contract. (Relationship: Company 1:N Contract)

departmentId.description: Reference to the Department responsible for the contract. (Relationship: Department 1:N Contract)

Document.title: Document
Document.description: Represents the full text content of a contract document.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Document entity.

content.description: The full text content of the contract document.

fileType.description: The file type of the document (e.g., 'pdf', 'docx', 'txt').

uploadDate.description: The date and time when the document was uploaded.

Company.title: Company
Company.description: Represents a company that is a party to a contract.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Company entity.

contactEmail.description: The contact email address for the company.

Department.title: Department
Department.description: Represents a department within the organization that manages contracts.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Department entity.

description.description: A description of the department's role and responsibilities.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification related to a contract event (e.g., renewal, expiration).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

contractId.description: Reference to the Contract to which this notification belongs. (Relationship: Contract 1:N Notification)

triggerDate.description: The date on which the notification should be triggered.

message.description: The message content of the notification.

ClauseRiskAssessment.title: ClauseRiskAssessment
ClauseRiskAssessment.description: Represents the risk assessment of a specific clause within a contract.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ClauseRiskAssessment entity.

contractId.description: Reference to the Contract to which this assessment belongs. (Relationship: Contract 1:N ClauseRiskAssessment)

clauseText.description: The text of the clause being assessed.

riskScore.description: The risk score assigned to the clause (e.g., 0-100).

riskFactors.description: A description of the factors contributing to the risk score.

recommendation.description: A recommendation for mitigating the risk associated with the clause.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Sentinel application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

departmentId.description: Reference to the Department the user belongs to. (Relationship: Department 1:N User)

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure, scalable, and easily maintainable system for managing contracts. It leverages denormalization to achieve authorization independence and structural segregation to simplify security rules. User data is stored under `/users/{userId}`. Companies and Departments are stored in top-level collections, as are Contracts. Contract documents are stored in the `documents` subcollection of the `contracts` collection. Notifications and Risk Assessments are kept as subcollections of Contracts, with each document containing a denormalized copy of relevant contract data. This design enables efficient querying and avoids the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules, ensuring that authorization can be performed independently at each document level. Specifically, the design supports QAPs by segregating data with different access needs into distinct collections and subcollections and by denormalizing authorization data to prevent rules from acting as filters.
